mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 900K in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from the mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, depressing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates weakening manufacturing activity and reduces corporate revenue prospects, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.5 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of more than 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) within a single month signals a synchronized labor and supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous +0.5pp AND INDPRO < previous -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an extended monetary accommodation, supporting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND GDPC1 YoY change < 0% for six consecutive months
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation and negative GDP growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside a monthly unemployment rate below 5% signals a tight labor market, raising wage pressures and input costs, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 100000 AND UNRATE < 5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below the previous month for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < 0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
